pages.title: A community that changes over time

figures.caption: The Premium-100 solar calendar in 2024. Each column is one civil day and each row a local quarter-hour. Colour shows aggregate PV power. Seasonal daylight and day-to-day weather are visible in the inputs.
Residential/service composition and the scale of PV and stationary storage. Bubble area increases with connector count; exact totals are given in the table.
Household-size distributions and residential floor-area distributions. Boxes show the median and interquartile range; isolated boxplot outliers are hidden for readability.
Premium residential archetypes and mean opening hours by weekday in 2024. The opening-hour summary includes holidays; it is an average over actual civil days.

Premium ownership by member and asset-ownership shares across all four bases. The horizontal line after Premium member 080 separates households from services. Consumption-only means no PV, stationary battery, EV connector or controllable appliance.
The 2024 non-shiftable demand ledger and each member's annual load/PV position in its static base. These annual totals do not estimate self-consumption or grid exports.
Monthly mean non-shiftable demand per catalogue member. Dashed lines are 2023; solid lines are 2024. Dividing by days in each month avoids treating a longer month as higher daily demand.
Premium mean non-shiftable power per site in 2024, separated by residential/services and mutually exclusive day classes. Public holidays take precedence over weekend classification.
Cumulative 2024 non-shiftable demand, with members ranked from largest to smallest, and the eight largest Premium demand sites. The dotted line represents equal demand per member.
PV array nameplate capacity by base and Premium DC/AC ratings. Each point is an installation. The dotted line marks equal DC array and AC inverter ratings.

Premium monthly specific PV yield and mean January/July 2024 power profiles. Solid intraday curves show PV; dashed curves show non-shiftable load. They are descriptive averages, not a dispatch or sharing calculation.
Stationary battery capacities and energy/power pairs. Repeated products may overlap in the scatter plot; the table gives the exact counts.

Single/three-phase site proportions and the selected Core-30 import-limit changes in Safety. Points below the dotted line have a reduced limit; overlapping points correspond to repeated connection levels.
EV usable-capacity distributions and the split between resident vehicles and external visitors. Cumulative curves count vehicle identities, not charging sessions.
The ten Premium sites with the most connectors, and connector counts by rated charging power and phase assignment. all_phases denotes a three-phase connection.

Premium 2024 arrival and departure hours for complete sessions in the Normal input files. Histograms use one-hour bins in Lisbon civil time. Sessions crossing the start or end of the two-year record are excluded here.

Premium 2024 target-SOC bands and cumulative connection-duration distributions for complete sessions. The final SOC band is exactly 100%. The duration axis displays the first 36 hours; residential parking has a longer tail.

Mean fraction of Premium connectors with a vehicle connected, by local hour and weekday in 2024. Residential and service connectors use separate denominators. These are scheduled connections, not charging utilisation.
The four resident vehicle identities with a home-work link in Premium. Each edge joins a home member to the designated work member; repeated daily journeys are not drawn separately.

Illustrative Premium washing-machine and dishwasher programmes, and the energy/duration distribution of all controllable programme profiles. Powers are interval averages obtained from the stored quarter-hour cycle energy.

Allowed start-time slack in 2024: latest start minus earliest start. Left: distribution by base. Right: Premium weekday/weekend/holiday requests. Boxplots show medians, quartiles and non-outlier whiskers.
Active member trajectories and the Premium All-in asset inventory. Asset counts include only active members. The unchanged 2024 segment carries forward the state reached in 2023.
Two histories for member 001, with Lisbon civil timestamps. The matching member label belongs to a different base in each row; the dates are not assumed to be identical.

Development schedules across both years. Thin events are marked with points for visibility; marker width is not event duration. Core-30 Robustness has continuous measurement noise; Premium All-in has seasonal campaigns.

Premium All-in outage timing and cumulative scheduled site-hours in the three configurations containing outages. A site-hour counts one affected site for one hour; simultaneous sites are counted separately.

The operational-candidate requests in 2023 and 2024. Positive values request increased demand; negative values request a reduction. The separate 1,500 kW stress request is omitted from this axis to preserve the operational scale.
Daily mean price and carbon intensity over both years. Shading gives the within-day 10th-90th percentile. Price units are cents/kWh; carbon units are gCO2e/kWh.
Daily mean air temperature in both years and Premium daily PV energy in 2024. The PV record contains day-to-day fluctuations within the seasonal envelope.
